data.long_meaning: Arjita is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘arjita’, meaning precious, valuable, or conquered. In Hindu mythology, Arjita is a popular name for girls, inspired by the hero Arjuna from the Mahabharata. The name Arjita carries the meaning “Precious, Valuable” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arjita usually hope their child will grow to embody precious, valuable and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Arjita is a beautiful name that holds profound cultural importance in Hindu tradition. The name has a regal and majestic ring to it, reminiscent of the ancient heroes and mythological figures of Hindu lore. Arjuna, the great archer and the revered disciple of Lord Krishna, is a significant symbol of bravery, valor, and righteousness in Hindu culture. As a name, Arjita carries the legacy of Arjuna's heroic exploits and inspires a sense of pride and strength in those who bear it.
data.spiritual_significance: Arjita is a name with deep spiritual significance in Hindu philosophy. The name Arjuna itself denotes conqueror or the one who is invincible in battle. Arjita, meaning precious or valuable, signifies the inner worth and divine connection that lies within every individual. It encourages us to tap into our inner strength and conquer the fears and challenges that come our way. The name is a constant reminder to seek knowledge, wisdom, and enlightenment, and to live a life that is guided by righteous intentions and noble values. Empowering and meaningful, the name Arjita instills a deep sense of self-worth, confidence, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference:
Arjita was an important queen of the Satavahana Dynasty, ruling from around 130 AD to 165 AD.
Context: Arjita is believed to have ruled as a regent for her young son, Shatakarni II.

Arjita is also mentioned in the Mahabharata epic, as the name of a kingdom ruled by a Madhavaraja.
Context: The exact time period of this reference is not known, but it is believed to be before the Mahabharata war.
